label: ADVICE
title: What a real efficiency scheme would need
status: Roadmap only. Nothing here is built, reviewed or accepted by anyone.
caveat: This is our own reasoning, not advice from a lawyer or an auditor. We have not studied any specific standard yet, so we name none.

items.need: A methodology that outsiders have reviewed
items.why: Today the method is ours: paired runs, a Welch test, a bootstrap interval. A scheme needs people who do not work for us to read it, break it and sign off.
items.wattnot_has: A published receipt spec, a standalone verifier and conformance vectors.

items.why: A saving is only as honest as the thing it is measured against. If anyone can pick a flattering baseline, the number means nothing.
items.wattnot_has: Both arms are in the receipt, so a reader can see the baseline.
items.gap: No rule for what counts as a fair baseline across workloads.

items.why: A receipt we sign ourselves proves the file was not edited. It does not prove the run was honest.
items.wattnot_has: Signed receipts, with a public-log option (Rekor) that is off in this build.
items.gap: No independent party re-runs or audits.

items.need: A registry that prevents double counting
items.why: The same saving must not be certified twice or sold to two people.
items.wattnot_has: A local hash-chained register that blocks a second certificate for the same receipt, run or source.
items.gap: Local file only. One user can start a second register. A real one needs a shared, controlled ledger.

items.why: Whether such a statement may be traded, claimed in marketing or used in a report depends on the law where it is used.
items.wattnot_has: Wording rules that keep any carbon claim out, and a permanent MOCK watermark.
